# Domain Rules

<!-- Generated by /ai-context. Manual edits are overwritten on re-run. -->

## AS IS — Current state

### Overview

- **Training session** — one drill: chosen problem, duration, elapsed time, diagram, checklist marks, notes, capacity estimate. The only table the app writes at runtime (`app/Models/TrainingSession.php`).
- **Catalog** — 11 seeded, runtime-read-only tables that form the closed vocabulary: 14 problems, 6 component categories, 28 components, 9 link types, 5 phases, 25 checklist items, 3 durations, 2 estimate modes, 3 problem levels, 3 problem item types.
- **Derived state** — current session, save indicator, legend and phase slices are all computed, never stored. Connection order is the exception that proves the rule: it is stored on the edge (`edges[].order`), not derived from the drawing.
- **Two locks** — owner-scoped route binding + policy on every session action.
- **No evaluation** — nothing scores, grades or reviews a diagram (`tests/Feature/Sessions/NoDiagramEvaluationTest.php`).

### The catalog is versioned data, not runtime state

- `CatalogSeeder` calls 10 child seeders in dependency order: `ProblemLevel`, `ProblemItemType`, `SessionDuration`, `EstimateMode`, `LinkType`, `ComponentCategory`, `Component`, `Phase`, `ChecklistItem`, `Problem`.
- Every seeder uses `upsert` keyed by a natural key (`slug`, `minutes`, `(phase_id, position)`), so `php artisan db:seed --class=CatalogSeeder` is idempotent and never touches anyone's `training_sessions`.
- `app/Concerns/ReadOnlyAtRuntime.php` throws `RuntimeException` on `saving`/`deleting` unless `app()->runningInConsole()`. There is no CRUD route, no admin screen.
- Changing the domain = editing a seeder and re-seeding (`README.md`, "O catálogo é seedado, não editável pela interface").
- Cross-boundary constraint: `components.icon_key` must exist in `resources/js/canvas/icons.ts`; `ComponentSeeder` sets `icon_key` = component `slug`, and a PHP test greps the TS file to check it (`.ai/rules/seeders.md`).

### Deactivating a catalog row hides it without erasing old drawings

`is_active = false` removes an item from palettes and menus, but `CatalogService` re-admits exactly what the loaded session still references:

| Collection | Filter in `app/Services/CatalogService.php` |
| --- | --- |
| `problems` | `is_active = true` OR `id = $session->problem_id` |
| `components` | `is_active = true` OR `slug IN (session.nodes[].type)` |
| `component_categories` | `is_active = true` OR `id IN` categories of the admitted components |
| `link_types` | `is_active = true` OR `slug IN (session.edges[].kind)` |
| `phases` (+ `checklist_items`) | `active()` scope only |
| `session_durations`, `estimate_modes` | `active()` scope only |

`app/Concerns/HasActiveScope.php` provides the `active()` scope; `app/Models/Scopes/OrderByPosition.php` and `OrderByCategoryPosition.php` make `position` the default ordering everywhere, so catalog order is content, not accident.

### The current session is derived, never pointed at

- `CurrentSessionResolver::resolve(User)` returns `TrainingSession::ownedBy($user)->orderByDesc('last_opened_at')->orderByDesc('id')->first()`.
- No pointer column exists on `users`; the tie-break by `id` is the same one `TrainingSessionController::index()` uses, so the first row of the session sheet is always the current one.
- `POST /api/sessions/{id}/open` sets `last_opened_at = now()` — that single write is what "switching sessions" means; the previous session is left untouched.
- `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` deletes and then calls `resolve()` again: the next-most-recent session is promoted by consequence, and if none remains a fresh empty one is created.

### A session is born exactly one way

`app/Services/SessionCreator.php` is the single birth path (used by `store`, by `CurrentSessionResolver` and by nothing else):

| Field | Value at birth | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `problem_id` | `null` unless supplied | request |
| `session_duration_id` | row where `is_default = true` → 45 minutes | `SessionDurationSeeder` |
| `show_connection_order` | `true` — a new board opens with the numbering visible | constant (column default is `true` too) |
| `elapsed_seconds` | `0` | constant |
| `notes` | `null` | constant |
| `nodes` / `edges` / `checks` | `[]` | constant |
| `estimate` | `SessionCreator::DEFAULT_ESTIMATE` = `mode: user, dau: 1000000, act: 10, per_month: 10000000, ratio: 100, size: 1, peak: 3, ret: 3` | constant |
| `last_opened_at` | `now()` — makes it current immediately | constant |

A missing catalog throws: `'O catálogo de durações não tem a duração pedida — rode o CatalogSeeder.'`.

### Autosave contract and limits

`app/Http/Requests/TrainingSessionUpdateRequest.php` is the whole contract. Repairable input is normalized in `prepareForValidation()`; the rest is rejected with 422.

| Input | Behavior | Constant / rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| negative `estimate.*` numeric | normalized to `0` | `ESTIMATE_FIELDS` |
| `nodes[].label`, `edges[].kind`, `edges[].label` arriving as `null` | normalized back to `''` (undoes `ConvertEmptyStringsToNull`) | `withTextKeysBack()` |
| `nodes` count > 200 | 422 — "O diagrama comporta no máximo 200 blocos." | `MAX_NODES` |
| `edges` count > 400 | 422 — "O diagrama comporta no máximo 400 ligações." | `MAX_EDGES` |
| `nodes[].label` / `edges[].label` > 60 chars | 422 | `MAX_LABEL` |
| `notes` > 5000 chars | 422 | `MAX_NOTES` |
| `nodes[].type` not a `components.slug` | 422 — "Este componente não existe no catálogo." | `Rule::in` |
| `edges[].kind` not a `link_types.slug` and not `''` | 422 | `linkKinds()` (9 slugs + `''`) |
| `edges[].from` / `edges[].to` not an id present in `nodes` | 422 | `Rule::in($nodeIds)` |
| `edges[].to === edges[].from` | 422 — "Uma ligação precisa chegar a um bloco diferente do de origem." | `notTheSourceOfTheEdge()` |
| `edges[].order` not an integer in 1–400 | 422 — "A ordem da ligação começa em 1." / "…vai até 400." | `min:1`, `max:MAX_EDGES` |
| `edges[].order` repeated in the array | 422 — "Duas ligações não podem ter o mesmo número de ordem." | `orderIsUniqueInTheDiagram()` |
| `edges[].order` sparse (`[1, 3, 4]`) | **accepted** — density is the client's job, not a server rule | `densify()` in `resources/js/canvas/order.ts` |
| `edges[].order` `null` | accepted — the edge is simply outside the sequence | `nullable` |
| `show_connection_order` non-boolean | 422 | `boolean` |
| `checks` key not a `checklist_items.id` | 422 | `knownChecklistItems()` |
| `duration_minutes` outside seeded minutes | 422 — "A duração do treino é de 30, 45 ou 60 minutos." | `Rule::in(SessionDuration…minutes)` |
| `elapsed_seconds` < 0 | 422 | `min:0` |
| `user_id` in the payload | ignored — not in the rules, never reaches the model | `validated()` |

The same limits are mirrored client-side in `resources/js/canvas/limits.ts` (`MAX_NODES = 200`, `MAX_EDGES = 400`, `MAX_LABEL_LENGTH = 60`) so the engine refuses before the session goes dirty; the server refuses again because the client is not authority. To change a limit, edit the constants in both files — no migration is involved.

`app/Services/SessionStateWriter.php` writes JSON columns and own columns inside one `DB::transaction`, translating `duration_minutes` → `session_duration_id` and filling `show_connection_order` straight from the payload, so a session never holds half a drawing.

### Autosave timing and failure handling

`resources/js/prancheta/autosave.ts`:

| Trigger | Delay | Constant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local mirror to `localStorage` | 800 ms after last change | `LOCAL_SAVE_DELAY_MS` |
| Server `PUT` | 3000 ms after last change | `SERVER_SAVE_DELAY_MS` |
| Ceiling (clock ticking every 1 s would otherwise reset the debounce forever) | 15000 ms | `SERVER_SAVE_MAX_WAIT_MS` |
| `beforeunload` / `pagehide` | immediate local save | `bindUnload()` |

| Failure | Wait | Chip label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP 429 | `Retry-After` header × 1000, else 20000 ms | `aguardando para salvar` |
| Any other status, incl. network status `0` | `min(3000 × 2^(attempt-1), 48000)` | none |
| Cached `serverUpdatedAt` newer than the store's | no send at all | `versão mais nova na nuvem` |

Nothing is reverted or discarded on failure: the session stays dirty and the work stays on screen and in the browser. The save chip is derived (`saving` → `dirty` → `saved`), so the UI cannot claim "saved" over a changed payload.

### The clock is phase-weighted and always resumes paused

`resources/js/prancheta/clock.ts` holds only arithmetic — every weight, phase name and duration comes from the server.

| Phase (`database/seeders/PhaseSeeder.php`) | `weight` | Share of a 45-min drill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Requisitos & escopo | 0.110 | ~4.9 min |
| Estimativas de capacidade | 0.110 | ~4.9 min |
| API & modelo de dados | 0.180 | ~8.1 min |
| Desenho de alto nível | 0.270 | ~12.2 min |
| Escala & trade-offs | 0.330 | ~14.9 min |

- Weights sum to exactly 1.000, which is what makes the roteiro progress close at 100%.
- `bounds()` accumulates normalized weights and forces the last slice to end at the total, so rounding never leaks.
- `curPhase()` returns the first slice whose `end` exceeds elapsed; past the total the last phase stays open.
- `clockTone()`: `normal` → `warn` above `WARN_RATIO = 0.85` of the duration → `over` at or past the total.
- `SessionClock` starts paused by construction; it stops itself when the time is exhausted (`tick()` → `pause()`), persists elapsed to the browser every `CLOCK_PERSIST_MS = 20000`, and changing the duration recalculates slices without touching elapsed.

### Checklist marks are keyed by `checklist_items.id`

- `checks` is a `Record<string, boolean>` keyed by the catalog row id (`resources/js/prancheta/session.ts` `SessionChecks`), validated server-side by `knownChecklistItems()`.
- Absence means unchecked (`isChecked()` in `resources/js/prancheta/roteiro.ts`), so the map only carries what was ticked.
- `TrainingSessionResource` carries `#[PreserveKeys]`; without it the resource filter would reindex the numeric keys and item 7's mark would arrive as item 0's.
- The frozen prototype keyed by `"phase:index"`; this app deliberately keys by id because reordering or inserting an item in a seeder would otherwise reinterpret existing marks (`README.md` divergence table; `tests/Feature/DeliveryContractTest.php:172`).

### Connection order is explicit, one sequence per diagram

`resources/js/canvas/order.ts`: every edge carries its own number in `edges[].order` (`number | null`). The position in the `edges` array carries no meaning, there is no numbering mode, and nothing about the order is inferred from the shape of the drawing.

| Rule | Where |
| --- | --- |
| A diagram has exactly one sequence; `order = null` means "outside it" | `Edge.order` (`resources/js/canvas/types.ts`) |
| The non-null orders are always exactly `{1 … N}` — no gap, no repeat | `densify()`, the single exit point of every order mutation |
| A new edge is born unnumbered | `addEdge()` writes `order: null` (`canvas/diagram.ts`) |
| Setting an edge to `k` pushes whoever held `k` or more one number forward | `setOrder()` |
| Removing an edge or a block closes the gap once, at the end of the removal | `clearOrder()` / `removeEdge()` / `removeNode()` |
| An orphan edge (endpoint no longer drawn) keeps its number and counts toward `N`, but draws no badge | `densify()` sweeps all of `state.edges`; `liveEdges()` decides what is drawn |
| `bidir` is a drawing flag with no graph meaning — one edge, one number | `autoNumber()` walks `from → to` only |
| Automatic numbering is a deterministic BFS: clients without input first, then the remaining entry blocks, then every block | `autoNumber()` / `sequenceRoots()`, tie-broken by the `edges` array order |
| Each edge is walked once, which is what makes a cyclic diagram terminate | `breadthFirst()` |

`show_connection_order` is a per-session display flag, not diagram content: it hides every badge on screen and in the exported SVG while the numbers stay intact, it is persisted on `training_sessions`, and it never enters `DiagramSnapshot` — toggling it does not push an undo step. Every `order` mutation does, through `CanvasEngine.mutateEdge`, and automatic numbering pushes exactly one step for the whole diagram.

The number input in the connection panel commits on `change`/Enter/blur and clamps to `N` for an edge already in the sequence, `N + 1` for one joining it (`clampOrderInput()`); an empty field is a no-op — only the "remove from the sequence" button clears a number.

### Link types carry stroke and badge, never color

`database/seeders/LinkTypeSeeder.php` — 9 rows; `dash_array = null` means a solid stroke, and `gloss` is the teaching line the auto-legend prints under the badge.

| slug | badge | dash_array | bidirectional default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `http` | HTTP | — | no |
| `grpc` | gRPC | — | no |
| `ws` | WS | — | **yes** |
| `event` | async | `5 4.5` | no |
| `query` | query | — | no |
| `cache` | cache | — | no |
| `repl` | replica | `5 4.5` | no |
| `batch` | batch | `5 4.5` | no |
| `retry` | retry | `2 4.5` | no |

Color has exactly one source: `component_categories.color_token` (6 rows: `--c-client`, `--c-edge`, `--c-compute`, `--c-data`, `--c-async`, `--c-ops`). No other catalog table has a color column, and `ComponentResource` omits color on purpose — a block inherits its category's token. An edge with no chosen type is legitimate: kind `''` renders in the legend as `UNTYPED_NAME = 'sem tipo'` (`resources/js/canvas/legend.ts`).

### The legend is fully derived

`resources/js/canvas/legend.ts` has no own state and no configuration: sections are computed from the categories currently drawn, the link types the edges use, and whether the diagram has at least one numbered live edge with `show_connection_order` on. The sequence section's copy is the client-side pair `ORDER_NAME` / `ORDER_GLOSS` exported by the same module — a single constant, deliberately not a parallel catalog (`.ai/rules/canvas.md`). The exported SVG shows the same legend, produced by the same module, with a resolved `SvgPalette` (CSS token → color) because a downloaded file cannot read the document's variables — a missing token falls back to `currentColor`, never an empty attribute (`.ai/rules/canvas.md`).

### Capacity estimate: two input modes, one arithmetic

`resources/js/prancheta/estimate.ts`. The only branch is the first line; everything after is derived from writes/day, so equivalent inputs in either mode produce identical output.

| Mode slug | Own fields | writes/day |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user` | `dau`, `act` | `dau × act` |
| `month` | `per_month` | `per_month / 30` |

Shared fields in both modes (preserved on switch): `ratio` (reads per write), `size` (KB per record), `peak` (peak factor), `ret` (retention years).

Derived rows (10, always in this order): `writes_month`, `writes_day`, `write_qps`, `reads_day`, `read_qps`, `peak_qps`, `data_day`, `data_year`, `retention`, `outbound`.

- `readsPerDay = writesPerDay × ratio`; `writeQps = writesPerDay / 86400`; `peakQps = (writeQps + readQps) × peak`; `dataPerDayKb = writesPerDay × size`; `retentionKb = dataPerDayKb × 365 × ret`; `outboundKbPerSecond = readQps × peak × size`.
- `MONTH_DAYS = 30` is announced in the output note; `sanitize()` clamps every parameter to a finite value ≥ 0, so empty or absurd fields never yield `NaN`.
- Highlight: `ALWAYS_HIGHLIGHTED = ['peak_qps', 'retention']`, plus the row whose label matches the active mode's `estimate_modes.highlighted_row` ("Escritas por dia" for `user`, "Escritas por mês" for `month`).
- Conclusion thresholds: `peak_qps ≥ 50000` → "esse pico exige cache e particionamento…"; `≥ 5000` → "dá para servir com réplicas de leitura e cache"; below → "uma instância bem dimensionada aguenta, não invente complexidade".

To add a mode: seed the `estimate_modes` row (slug + `highlighted_row` label) and add its field list to `MODE_FIELDS`.

### Problems ship a statement and a post-drill answer key

`database/seeders/data/problems.php` holds 14 statements verbatim, each with `slug`, `name`, `tag`, `lv` (1/2/3 → `problem_levels` slugs `base`/`intermediate`/`advanced`), `context`, and three lists persisted as `problem_items` rows discriminated by `problem_item_types.slug`:

| `problem_item_types.slug` | Resource key | Shown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requirement` | `requirements` | with the statement |
| `scale` | `scale` | with the statement |
| `topic` | `topics` | only in the collapsed answer-key block after the drill |

Slugs: `url`, `feed`, `chat`, `video`, `ride`, `drive`, `rate`, `notif`, `typeahead`, `tickets`, `crawler`, `metrics`, `pay`, `leaderboard`. `ProblemResource` splits the three lists from one eager-loaded relation (no query per list) and exposes the level three ways (`level`, `level_name`, `level_position`) because the UI paints the level step from its position.

### Authentication scope

`config/fortify.php` `features`: `registration`, `emailVerification`, `twoFactorAuthentication(confirm: true, confirmPassword: true)`, `passkeys(confirmPassword: true)`. `Features::resetPasswords()` is commented out — password recovery is out of v1 (`.ai/rules/config.md`). No route requires `verified`: `routes/settings.php` states the account is usable from birth. Post-auth destination `/prancheta` is declared twice and must stay in sync — `config/fortify.php` `'home' => '/prancheta'` and `bootstrap/app.php` `$middleware->redirectUsersTo('/prancheta')` (`.ai/rules/routes.md`).
